title: Impact of New Seed Variety Adoption on Farm Income

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Instrumental Variables (2SLS).
- Rationale: Adoption of the new seed variety (x) is likely endogenous to income (y) due to selection on unobservables (e.g., managerial ability, risk preferences, expected shocks). Agroecological suitability (z) affects the incentive and feasibility to adopt but, conditional on other farm characteristics (controls), is plausibly unrelated to unobserved determinants of income except through adoption.
- Key assumptions:
  - Relevance: Cov(z, x | controls) ≠ 0. Suitability must strongly predict adoption (verified via first-stage F-statistic).
  - Exclusion/Exogeneity: z affects income only through adoption after conditioning on controls, i.e., E[z · ε | controls] = 0.
  - Monotonicity: Suitability weakly increases adoption for all farms (no defiers), so the 2SLS identifies a LATE for compliers.
  - SUTVA and stable composition: No spillovers across farms and consistent construction of variables across observations.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code that:
# - Reads the CSV file from the path provided
# - Runs the appropriate causal analysis
# - Prints a clear numerical result (coefficient, CAR, etc.)
# - Includes basic robustness checks

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  ok <- requireNamespace("AER", quietly = TRUE) &&
        requireNamespace("sandwich", quietly = TRUE) &&
        requireNamespace("lmtest", quietly = TRUE)
  if (!ok) {
    stop("Please ensure packages AER, sandwich, and lmtest are installed.")
  }
  library(AER)
  library(sandwich)
  library(lmtest)
})

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s79_data.csv"
dat <- read.csv(path)
dat <- na.omit(dat)

# Ensure instrument is numeric 0/1
dat$z <- as.numeric(dat$z)

n <- nrow(dat)

# Helper to extract robust results for a coefficient
robust_stats <- function(model, varname) {
  ct <- lmtest::coeftest(model, vcov = sandwich::vcovHC(model, type = "HC1"))
  if (!(varname %in% rownames(ct))) stop(paste("Variable", varname, "not found in model."))
  b  <- ct[varname, 1]
  se <- ct[varname, 2]
  t  <- ct[varname, 3]
  p  <- ct[varname, 4]
  ci_low  <- b - 1.96 * se
  ci_high <- b + 1.96 * se
  list(beta = as.numeric(b), se = as.numeric(se), t = as.numeric(t), p = as.numeric(p),
       ci_low = as.numeric(ci_low), ci_high = as.numeric(ci_high))
}

cat("Sample size (N):", n, "\n\n")

# 2) Naive OLS (y ~ x + controls)
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = dat)
ols_x <- robust_stats(ols, "x")
cat("Naive OLS (y ~ x + controls):\n")
cat(sprintf("  beta_OLS = %.4f, SE = %.4f, t = %.2f, p = %.4f, 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f]\n\n",
            ols_x$beta, ols_x$se, ols_x$t, ols_x$p, ols_x$ci_low, ols_x$ci_high))

# 3) First stage: x ~ z + controls
fs <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = dat)
fs_z <- robust_stats(fs, "z")
F_fs <- fs_z$t^2  # robust F for single coefficient
cat("First-stage (x ~ z + controls):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Effect of z on x: pi1 = %.4f, SE = %.4f, t = %.2f, p = %.4f\n", fs_z$beta, fs_z$se, fs_z$t, fs_z$p))
cat(sprintf("  Robust first-stage F (z): %.2f  (rule-of-thumb > 10 indicates strong instrument)\n\n", F_fs))

# 4) Reduced form: y ~ z + controls
rf <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = dat)
rf_z <- robust_stats(rf, "z")
cat("Reduced form (y ~ z + controls):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Effect of z on y: RF = %.4f, SE = %.4f, t = %.2f, p = %.4f\n\n",
            rf_z$beta, rf_z$se, rf_z$t, rf_z$p))

# 5) 2SLS (IV): y ~ x + controls | controls + z
iv <- AER::ivreg(y ~ x + controls | controls + z, data = dat)
iv_x <- robust_stats(iv, "x")
cat("2SLS (IV) main specification (y ~ x + controls | controls + z):\n")
cat(sprintf("  beta_IV = %.4f, SE = %.4f, z = %.2f, p = %.4f, 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f]\n\n",
            iv_x$beta, iv_x$se, iv_x$t, iv_x$p, iv_x$ci_low, iv_x$ci_high))

# Wu-Hausman endogeneity test (from AER diagnostics)
iv_sum <- summary(iv, diagnostics = TRUE)
# The diagnostics table may have row names "Wu-Hausman" or "Wu-Hausman test"
diag_tab <- iv_sum$diagnostics
if (!is.null(diag_tab)) {
  # Try to find Wu-Hausman row
  rn <- rownames(diag_tab)
  wh_idx <- which(grepl("Wu", rn, ignore.case = TRUE))
  if (length(wh_idx) > 0) {
    wh <- diag_tab[wh_idx[1], , drop = FALSE]
    stat <- as.numeric(wh[1,1]); pval <- as.numeric(wh[1,4])
    cat(sprintf("Wu-Hausman endogeneity test: statistic = %.3f, p = %.4f\n\n", stat, pval))
  }
}

# 6) Robustness checks

# 6a) IV without controls
iv_noc <- AER::ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = dat)
iv_noc_x <- robust_stats(iv_noc, "x")
cat("Robustness IV (no controls): y ~ x | z\n")
cat(sprintf("  beta_IV_noc = %.4f, SE = %.4f, z = %.2f, p = %.4f, 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f]\n\n",
            iv_noc_x$beta, iv_noc_x$se, iv_noc_x$t, iv_noc_x$p, iv_noc_x$ci_low, iv_noc_x$ci_high))

# 6b) IV with richer controls (quadratic in controls)
iv_quad <- AER::ivreg(y ~ x + controls + I(controls^2) | controls + I(controls^2) + z, data = dat)
iv_quad_x <- robust_stats(iv_quad, "x")
# First-stage with quadratic controls to reassess instrument strength
fs_quad <- lm(x ~ z + controls + I(controls^2), data = dat)
fs_quad_z <- robust_stats(fs_quad, "z")
F_fs_quad <- fs_quad_z$t^2

cat("Robustness IV (quadratic controls): y ~ x + controls + controls^2 | z + controls + controls^2\n")
cat(sprintf("  beta_IV_quad = %.4f, SE = %.4f, z = %.2f, p = %.4f, 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            iv_quad_x$beta, iv_quad_x$se, iv_quad_x$t, iv_quad_x$p, iv_quad_x$ci_low, iv_quad_x$ci_high))
cat(sprintf("  First-stage (with quadratic controls) F for z: %.2f\n\n", F_fs_quad))

# Final clear numerical result
cat("Main causal estimate (preferred 2SLS):\n")
cat(sprintf("  beta_IV = %.4f (SE = %.4f), 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            iv_x$beta, iv_x$se, iv_x$ci_low, iv_x$ci_high))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Agroecologically suitable areas facilitate adoption, and improved seed varieties typically raise yields and thus farm income. After isolating exogenous variation in adoption using suitability, the IV estimate should be positive.
- Magnitude: Moderate to large. Given variables appear roughly standardized in the preview, a 1-unit increase in adoption intensity is expected to increase income by about 0.5 to 1.0 standard deviations. OLS may differ due to selection; if more capable farmers adopt earlier, OLS could be upward biased; if adoption is targeted to worse-off farms, OLS could be downward biased. The IV estimate addresses this and should lie within the 0.5–1.0 range if the instrument is strong (first-stage F > 10).

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use agroecological suitability as an instrument for new seed variety adoption.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Adopting the new seed variety leads to a significant increase in farm income.
